standard_prerequisites.name: The placement of the ideal in an associated prime when the depth against it is zero
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked in the base case (source lines 1941-1945)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a nonzero homomorphism out of the quotient by the ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of local cohomology as the colimit of the Ext modules out of the quotients by the powers of the ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked at the end of the counted proof (source lines 1989-1990)
standard_prerequisites.use: Compares the vanishing of local cohomology with the vanishing of those Ext modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: The finiteness of Ext modules out of a finite module over the quotient
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the induction step (source lines 1957-1959)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the long exact sequence into short exact sequences by Nakayama.

standard_prerequisites.name: The invariance of the depth under replacing the ideal by its powers
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source line 1971)
standard_prerequisites.use: Extends the vanishing statement to all powers of the ideal.

core_obligations: First equality: induct on the depth; in the base case the ideal lies in an associated prime, so a homomorphism out of the quotient by the ideal is nonzero, and in the induction step divide by a nonzerodivisor in the ideal, use finiteness of the Ext modules to read the connecting map as an isomorphism and the long exact sequence as short exact sequences (proof lines 1936-1968)

The additional statement: since the depth is unchanged when the ideal is replaced by its powers, the Ext modules out of the quotients by all powers vanish below the depth, and a presentation of a module killed by a power of the ideal transfers this vanishing by induction (proof lines 1970-1985)

Third equality: local cohomology is the colimit of those Ext modules, so it vanishes below the depth, and in the critical degree the map from the Ext module out of the quotient by the ideal into local cohomology is injective, which gives nonvanishing there (proof lines 1987-1995)
proof_roadmap: (1)=(2): induct on depth_I(M). Base: depth 0 means I lies in an associated prime p (via prime avoidance), so Hom_A(A/I, M) is nonzero. Step: choose a nonzerodivisor f in I, use the short exact sequence M -> M -> M/fM, finiteness of Ext^i_A(A/I, M) as A/I-modules, and the resulting short exact sequences to induct.

(additional statement): depth_I(M) = depth_{I^n}(M), so Ext^i_A(A/I^n, M)=0 below the depth; a module N killed by I^n is presented from (A/I^n)^m, and dimension shifting by induction gives Ext^i_A(N, M) = 0 below the depth.

(3): H^p_I(M) = colim Ext^p_A(A/I^n, M), so it vanishes below the depth; in degree equal to the depth the map Ext^i_A(A/I, M) -> H^i_I(M) is injective (using vanishing of Ext^{i-1}_A(I/I^n, M)), which gives nonvanishing.
difficulty_reason: The counted statement identifies three integers attached to a finite module over a Noetherian ring and an ideal: the depth against the ideal, the smallest degree in which Ext out of the quotient by the ideal is nonzero, and the smallest degree in which local cohomology is nonzero, and adds a vanishing statement for Ext out of any module killed by a power of the ideal below the depth (author lemma at source lines 1920-1933, label lemma-depth). The proof (source lines 1935-1996) runs an induction on the depth using finiteness of the Ext modules and the long exact sequence to obtain short exact sequences, transfers the vanishing to all powers of the ideal and then to modules killed by such powers by dimension shifting, and compares the colimit description of local cohomology with those Ext modules to finish (proof lines 1987-1995). The induction and the colimit comparison are the substance. H3.
